name: .500 Revolver Maximum
description:
The .500 Revolver Maximum is what happens when ammunition engineers stop asking 'should we?' and commit fully to 'can we?' The round is the commercial ceiling for handheld revolver cartridges in GLMZ 2200 — a half-inch diameter projectile launched at velocities that produce muzzle energies in the range of light rifle cartridges. The 'Maximum' designation was applied by Kovash Munitions to distinguish their extended-length load from shorter .500 revolver loads, and it stuck as a street name for the category. Modern production uses a steel-reinforced brass case and a pressure-optimized slow-burning propellant that produces a long, sustained push rather than a sharp spike — which is the difference between a weapon that cracks frames and one that merely destroys the shooter's wrist over time.

The cultural weight of this round in GLMZ 2200 is disproportionate to how many people actually carry it. It's the round that gets mentioned in enforcement circles as the theoretical answer to anything short of a full combat exoskeleton. It's what the outer-ring collectors buy when they want something that makes other collectors go quiet. It's also genuinely useful in the industrial collapse zones where the threats have sometimes been augmented beyond the point where a service pistol round is a reliable solution. Halverson produces the H-500 'Terminus' revolver specifically for this round; waiting lists run six to eight months and the price starts at Φ4,200 for a base model.
compatibility_note: Compatible only with revolvers specifically engineered for .500 Maximum pressure and case length, including the Halverson H-500 'Terminus' and Kovash K-500 platforms. Will not fit in standard .44 or .454 cylinders. Single-shot hunting pistols in this caliber exist but are rare. No semi-automatic platform compatibility.
reliability_note: Steel-reinforced brass case, maximum-pressure gunpowder load. Round-level reliability is excellent; weapon longevity is the primary concern — even purpose-built revolvers require barrel and cylinder inspection after sustained use. Functions in all weather and EMP conditions. Produces concussive muzzle blast. No electronic dependency.
